channel.title: lowob News Desk
channel.description: Dated regulation, platform and market news for AI, fintech, crypto and media, each tied to the lowob research that explains what it means.

item.title: Law firms read the OCC's new AI examiner framework
item.description: Outside counsel are already telling banks what examiners will ask for. Expect the questions to land on vendors before they land on policy. Source: Arnold & Porter.

item.title: Zapier surveys 513 US leaders on AI agents
item.description: A vendor survey, so read it as direction rather than proof. It is useful for the gap between agents planned and agents running in production. Source: Zapier.

item.title: Edelman and LinkedIn on what executives do with thought leadership
item.description: The measure that matters is what a reader does next, not whether they read. That is the bar for every piece we publish. Source: Edelman.

item.title: OCC publishes Bulletin 2026-54, an examiner framework for bank AI
item.description: It is examiner guidance and sets no new expectations for banks on its own. It still tells you which records an exam will ask to see. Source: OCC.

item.title: CMI and MarketingProfs publish the 2026 B2B content trends
item.description: A survey of 1,132 marketers, mostly in North America. Read it for where budgets are moving, not for what works. Source: Content Marketing Institute.

item.title: Menlo Ventures publishes its 2026 State of Enterprise AI
item.description: Nearly 400 enterprise buyers on where AI spend is going. Menlo invests in AI companies, so weigh it against buyer-side data. Source: Menlo Ventures.

item.title: Ahrefs measures how stable AI citations are
item.description: About 37,500 citations tracked over 20 days. Being cited once is not the same as being cited next week, so track it. Source: Ahrefs.

item.title: AICPA proposes updated SOC 2 trust services criteria
item.description: An exposure draft, so the criteria can still change. AI vendors in security review should know it is coming. Source: AICPA and CIMA.

item.title: First harmonised standard published under the EU AI Act
item.description: EN 18286 turns parts of the Act into something an auditor can check. Firms working towards ISO 42001 should map the overlap. Source: Orrick.

item.title: US bank regulators ask whether lenders can stop their AI agents
item.description: The question is shifting from whether a model is accurate to whether someone can halt it. The kill switch is becoming a control. Source: ComplexDiscovery.

item.title: Meta reports third-quarter 2026 results
item.description: Price per ad reflects performance and mix as well as competition. Read the change carefully before blaming the auction. Source: Meta.

item.title: Google to require licence proof from US and Canadian financial advertisers in 2027
item.description: Exact dates and scope are not yet published. Fintechs that rely on paid search should start gathering licence evidence now. Source: PPC Land.

item.title: European Commission updates its AI literacy questions and answers
item.description: Official guidance, not law, but it sets the date supervision starts. An acceptable use policy plus training records is the practical answer. Source: European Commission.

item.title: FCA sets out good and poor practice for AI in financial services
item.description: Examples only, with no new rules. It is still the clearest public list of what the UK regulator wants to see. Source: FCA.

item.title: Q3 2026 venture data: billion-dollar rounds mask a narrowing market
item.description: Headline totals are carried by a few very large rounds. Most companies are raising in a tighter market than the totals suggest. Source: Foley & Lardner.

item.title: Bloomberg launches Enterprise MCP for AI data access
item.description: Licensed market data is now reachable by agents through a standard connector. Check the licence before you check the latency. Source: IT Brief UK.

item.title: Reuters: banking watchdogs step up AI scrutiny
item.description: Based on unnamed sources, so treat it as a signal. It fits the run of examiner guidance that followed in November. Source: Reuters via Khaleej Times.

item.title: Google folds enterprise AI into a single Gemini agent
item.description: Suite vendors are bundling memory and context into the agent. The open question is whether your decisions stay readable outside it. Source: Futurum Group.

item.title: AWS on access control for retrieval with Amazon Quick and Bedrock
item.description: Vendor-written, but a useful pattern: the retriever should only see what the person asking is allowed to see. Source: AWS Machine Learning Blog.

item.title: The CLARITY Act stalls in the Senate
item.description: US market structure stays unsettled into 2027. Token decisions should work without counting on it passing. Source: Orrick.

item.title: WFA study: global brands move away from paying agencies for time
item.description: Fees tied to outputs and outcomes are replacing hours. Ask any agency what the fee is tied to before you sign. Source: VideoWeek.

item.title: IAB Tech Lab finalises podcast measurement v2.3, now covering video
item.description: Video podcasts finally have a shared counting rule. Ask sponsors which version their numbers follow. Source: PPC Land.

item.title: KPMG Q3 2026 AI Pulse survey
item.description: Large-company leaders on agent deployment. Useful as a benchmark for how far peers have actually got. Source: KPMG.

item.title: BLS publishes Employee Tenure in 2026
item.description: People move on faster than decisions expire. That is the case for writing down why, not just what. Source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics.

item.title: IAB Europe: agentic ad buying gains ground
item.description: An industry survey summary without a stated sample size. A signal of direction for publishers, not a measure. Source: ExchangeWire.
